title: What is known about 1RB1LF_0RC1RC_1LD0RD_0LE0LA_1RA0LB_---1LD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LF_0RC1RC_1LD0RD_0LE0LA_1RA0LB_---1LD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. This machine is proved in Lean to halt from blank tape exactly when its twin 1RB1LE_1RC1LF_0RD1RD_1LE0RE_0LA0LB_---1LE halts from blank tape started in state B. The twin's own question is its run from state A, a different run, so the two holdouts remain two questions; the twin's analysis has not yet produced a decision.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 70,552 cells have been visited and 48,004 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.482). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.046).

claims.title: The counter rounds, for all run lengths
claims.text: Six rounds from one left-end visit to the next: the digit next to the left end goes 0→1→2→3, and 3 wraps to 0 with a carry into the next digit (0, 1 or 2), for all lengths of the runs of pairs and any tape to the right.

claims.title: The timers
claims.text: At the right-end visits (counter overflows) the last block loses 9 ones, the one before it 24, the one before that 96, the next about 384 (C simulation to 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps, no halt).

claims.title: It is the twin, started in state B
claims.text: Renaming the states, every transition agrees with 1RB1LE_1RC1LF_0RD1RD_1LE0RE_0LA0LB_---1LE except E1 → 0LB, which with the next two steps does what the twin’s A1 → 1LE does in one. So this machine halts from blank tape if and only if the twin halts from blank tape started in state B (and likewise from every configuration).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known; by the twin theorem it is the same question as for the twin started in state B (see that machine’s page for the right-end map and what is missing).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine runs a base-4 counter at the left end of its tape; each overflow sends the head to a stack of timers on the right, which run down at rates 9, 24, 96, … This page runs the real machine and explains the counter.

facts.text: The counter's rounds, proved for all run lengths.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.482). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.046).
After 109 steps the tape spans 70,552 cells (48,802 left of the start, 97 right), with a density of 1s of 0.68.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A base-4 counter
html: At each visit of the left end (state D) the tape begins (110)^n0 d0 (110)^n1 d1 …, each digit d one of 10, 1, 101, 11 (0 to 3). One round adds one:
The first run of pairs grows by one per round, so the left part grows like the square root of time; a carry out of digit i happens once every 4i+1 rounds.

sections.heading: Timers that run down
html: When the carry runs off the last digit, the head sweeps on to the right end, through long blocks of ones. At each such visit the last block loses 9 ones, the one before it 24, the next 96, the next about 384; when a timer is exhausted it is refilled from the blocks on its left. Overflows come exponentially rarely, so this side of the tape grows like a logarithm.

The machine halts exactly at the pattern F0: it happens when D reads a 1 whose left neighbour is a 1 with a 0 before it (`0 1 D>1` gives `D1 -> 0LA`, `A1 -> 1LF`, F on the 0); whether a refill ever produces it is the open question. Its twin 1RB1LE_1RC1LF_0RD1RD_1LE0RE_0LA0LB_---1LE behaves the same way with a different last timer.

sections.heading: The twin's table, started in state B
html: Rename the twin’s states A–F to E, A, B, C, D, F. Every transition then matches this machine except one: the twin’s A1 → 1LE becomes E1 → 0LB here, and B (which writes back what it reads, moving right) followed by C0 → 1LD undoes the 0 and lands one cell left in D. Three steps for one, so halting is preserved in both directions; lean/Twin.lean proves it for every configuration.
From blank tape this machine starts where the twin would be in state B, so the twin’s first step (which writes one extra 1) is the whole difference between the two runs.

summary: A base-4 counter with timers; proved to halt from blank tape exactly when its twin 1RB1LE_1RC1LF_0RD1RD_1LE0RE_0LA0LB_---1LE halts from blank tape in state B.
